summary: Iteration 3 validates the chat redirect + real chat behaviour. Backend: 28/28 pytest tests pass (3 new) — GET /api/chats/participating excludes cards the user owns and only returns cards they actually have a chat row on (also returns success:true, cards:[] for a brand-new user). POST /api/chats now persists is_from_owner exactly as supplied (round-tripped via GET — owner-msg=true, friend-msg=false). All 25 pre-existing tests (auth/cards/chats/notifications) still pass. Frontend E2E (live preview URL, /sorry-kitty.html#card=jj0WBUwwdMj): (1) kOpenChat() stores sessionStorage['sk_pending_chat']=jj0WBUwwdMj when unauthenticated and slides up panel-auth; (2) signup as new friend → moment-window.open present, sender 'QA User' in top bar, sessionStorage['sk_pending_chat'] cleared, window.location.hash cleared; (3) login path also redirects friend.api@example.com directly into the same card's moment-window; (4) sendMoment() persists message with is_from_owner=false (verified via GET /api/chats); (5) no simulated reply — chat row count stays the same 5.5s after the friend sends (simulateMomentReply removed); (6) cross-session polling works — owner-side POST via API surfaces in the friend's moment-msg-zone within 3s as a 'THEM' bubble; (7) friend's Chat tab renders the participated card ('Moment with QA User') even though the friend owns 0 cards; clicking it re-opens the moment-window.

minor.issue: Still no auth check — any caller can write a message with any participant_id/is_from_owner. Acceptable for current spec but worth noting.
No auth check — anyone with a user_id can list that user's participated cards. Low risk (only returns public card rows).
Error paths return 200+{error:..} instead of 4xx; PATCH /api/cards bypasses ownership when user_id omitted; GET /api/notifications returns bare array (no envelope).

issues: UI is single-floating-bubble (showMoment) rather than a scrollable thread — only the latest message from either side is visible. By design per code, but the spec language ('chat actually load history') could read as a thread. Initial poll does show the last message from the other side so the friend has context.

action_items: (optional) Consider authenticating /api/chats POST + /api/chats/participating with the user's JWT instead of trusting client-supplied user_id/participant_id.
(carried) Return 4xx for auth/validation errors; require user_id on PATCH /api/cards; normalize GET /api/notifications envelope.
critical_code_review_comments: 06-moments.js pollMomentMessages: clean dedup via momentSeenIds + 3s setInterval. Initial poll shows the most-recent OTHER-side message so the friend lands with context, then subsequent polls only show new other-side messages — exactly the spec.
sendMoment correctly sets is_from_owner = (momentOwnerId === CU.id) and stores its own message id in momentSeenIds so the next poll doesn't echo it back.
simulateMomentReply function still EXISTS in 06-moments.js (line 510) but is no longer called from sendMoment / fireEmojiReaction. Dead code — safe but should be removed.

kOpenChat (08-card-viewer.js) and initApp dispatcher (03-app-init.js) cleanly hand off via sessionStorage['sk_pending_chat']; hash is cleared on success which prevents bouncing back into the public viewer on refresh.
renderChats now merges owned + participating cards (de-duped by id) and works for friends who own 0 cards.
06-moments.js is approaching 576 lines — consider splitting the moments UI from the chat-list rendering.
Backend /api/chats/participating cleanly uses an `in.(id,...)` filter + `owner_id=neq.<user>` — correct.
updated_files: /app/backend/tests/test_sorry_kitty.py (+3 tests: is_from_owner persistence, participating endpoint excludes-owned/includes-participated, empty for new user)

success_rate.frontend: 100% on all 7 iteration-3 E2E checks (signup redirect, login redirect, send persists with is_from_owner=false, no fake reply, 3s cross-session polling, Chat-tab participant list, click-to-reopen)

test_credentials: Demo sender: qa.user@example.com / password123. Returning friend: friend.api@example.com / password123. Tests also create ephemeral e2e_friend_<ts>@example.com signups.
seed_data_creation: Created additional chat rows on card jj0WBUwwdMj (owned by qa.user@example.com): friend pings + 'owner replies <ts>' messages, plus one fresh ephemeral friend e2e_friend_<ts>@example.com that now has a participating row on jj0WBUwwdMj.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend tests run with: pytest backend/tests/test_sorry_kitty.py -v --junitxml=/app/test_reports/pytest/pytest_results.xml. Key flows: (a) public share URL /sorry-kitty.html#card=<id> → kOpenChat() global → if unauth, panel-auth shows and sessionStorage['sk_pending_chat']=<id>; (b) after auth, initApp checks sk_pending_chat and calls openMomentWindow(pending) with 120ms setTimeout, clears the hash, removes the storage; (c) moment-window UI is a SINGLE floating bubble (showMoment) — polling at 3s replaces it with the latest other-side message. Don't expect a scrollable thread. Use #moment-msg-zone for the visible bubble. (d) renderChats merges DB.getCards(CU.id) + DB.getParticipatingCards(CU.id) — works for non-owners. (e) is_from_owner is persisted exactly as supplied by /api/chats; participating endpoint filters owner_id neq self.
rca of the issue: n/a — all iteration-3 requirements implemented correctly. Initial E2E run miscounted bubbles because the moments UI is by-design a single floating bubble (not a thread); re-run with #moment-msg-zone proved the cross-session message delivery works in ~3s via polling.
